stem: A $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ particle has resultant force $18\,\mathrm{N}$ in the positive direction. Calculate its acceleration.
A $4\,\mathrm{kg}$ particle has forces $8\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$ newtons. Calculate the magnitude of its acceleration.
Masses $2$ kg and $6$ kg hang on either side of a light string over a smooth fixed pulley, with $m2>m1$. Calculate their acceleration magnitude. Take $g=9.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
A $3$ kg particle slides down a smooth plane inclined at $60$ degrees to the horizontal. Calculate its acceleration down the plane. Take $g=9.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
A $3$ kg particle changes velocity from $2$ to $5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ along a chosen positive line. Calculate the signed impulse on it.
A $3$ kg particle moves right at $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and collides directly with a stationary $4$ kg particle. They stick together. Calculate their common speed after collision.
A $3$ kg particle slides on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $0.3$. Calculate the friction magnitude. Take $g=9.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

A $4$ kg particle slides down a rough plane inclined at $45$ degrees to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is $0.1$. Calculate its acceleration down the plane. Take $g=9.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
A 4 kg particle experiences a resultant force of 28 N along $\mathbf i$. Find its acceleration magnitude.
Masses 1 kg and 4 kg hang over a smooth fixed pulley. Find their acceleration magnitude.
A 2 kg particle moving right at 6 m s^-1 sticks to a stationary 4 kg particle. Find their common speed.
A 3 kg particle slides down a rough 30 degree plane with coefficient of friction 0.1. Find its acceleration.
